headline: A wet frontal passage cools Central Kentucky today; heavy-rain potential shifts into the Upstate this weekend
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A slow cold front brings widespread showers and a few embedded thunderstorms to Danville and the Bluegrass today, followed by a much cooler northeast flow this weekend. Rain tapers Saturday morning for most of the area, and Sunday trends mainly dry outside a small early shower chance.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: Locally heavy rain and isolated thunder; severe-weather risk is low
days.forecast: Showers expand from west to east this morning and become widespread by midday, with a few embedded thunderstorms possible. Temperatures briefly approach 80 before the front passes, then fall toward 70 during the afternoon. West wind turns north to northeast. Most locations receive around 0.5–1 inch, with isolated totals near 1.5 inches possible.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: Wet roads and lingering morning showers; no organized severe-weather threat
days.forecast: A chance of showers lingers through midmorning, especially south and southeast of Danville, before most of the Bluegrass becomes partly sunny. A steady northeast wind around 7–11 mph keeps temperatures in the upper 60s to near 70. Mostly cloudy conditions return Saturday night with only a slight shower chance.

days.label: Sunday
days.forecast: A stray early shower cannot be ruled out, mainly south of Danville, followed by a partly sunny and seasonably cool afternoon. Light northeast wind continues. Sunday night turns drier and cooler, with sheltered locations falling into the upper 40s.

kentucky.bottomLine: Today is the wettest period, with widespread rain and a low-end thunder risk but little support for severe storms. Rain diminishes Saturday morning, and most of Sunday is dry. The main change after the front is a drop from near 80 today to highs near 70 this weekend, followed by a cool Sunday night.
kentucky.confidence: High for today's rain and weekend cooling; moderate on the exact southern edge and duration of lingering weekend showers

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Clemson and Central stay hot and mainly dry today, but a back-door cold front and deep tropical moisture bring a sharp change this weekend. Showers and thunderstorms increase Saturday afternoon, with widespread rain and localized flooding potential Saturday night through Sunday.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: Unseasonable heat; an isolated mountain storm is possible well northwest of Clemson
days.forecast: Morning clouds give way to mostly sunny skies, with temperatures climbing into the upper 80s. Wind remains light from the southwest. Clemson and Central should stay dry through most or all of tonight, while isolated convection remains focused closer to the mountains.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: Locally heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms may produce localized flooding
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy and still warm early, then showers and thunderstorms become increasingly likely from midday into the evening as a back-door front settles south. Rain becomes widespread Saturday night. A general 0.75–1.5 inches is possible by Sunday morning, but placement is uncertain and locally higher totals cannot be ruled out.

days.label: Sunday
days.hazard: Localized flooding possible where repeated heavy showers occur
days.forecast: Cloudy, much cooler and wet under a developing northeast-flow wedge. Periods of rain continue, with a few embedded thunderstorms possible. Repeated showers could produce localized flooding, although the exact axis of heaviest rain remains uncertain. Rain continues into Sunday night before gradually easing toward Monday morning.

upstate.bottomLine: Today is the final hot and mostly dry day. Rain chances rise sharply Saturday afternoon, with the wettest period expected Saturday night through Sunday. Temperatures fall from the upper 80s today to near 70 Sunday. The heavy-rain setup is credible, but confidence in exact totals and the narrow flooding corridor remains lower than confidence in widespread rain.
upstate.confidence: High today; moderate for weekend timing and temperatures; moderate-low on exact heavy-rain placement and totals

sourceNotes: NWS point forecasts for Danville and Clemson were generated at approximately 6:20 AM EDT. Official airport observations span 5:55–6:00 AM EDT.

The Louisville and Greenville-Spartanburg Area Forecast Discussions were issued at 3:00 AM and 2:11 AM EDT, respectively. Louisville supports widespread Friday rain, 0.5–1 inch for most with isolated totals near 1.5 inches, low severe potential and a cooler weekend. Greenville-Spartanburg supports a hot dry Friday followed by widespread weekend rain, a Sunday cold-air-damming wedge and a Marginal excessive-rain risk with low confidence in exact totals.

The NWS active-alert API returned no active alerts for either the Danville or Clemson forecast point at the approximately 6:20 AM EDT check. This official-alert status is separate from the independent analysis.

Model inventories checked at 6:21 AM EDT showed the 09Z HRRR through forecast hour 15, 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 189, and the 06Z GEFS mean through hour 81. The latest complete ECMWF deterministic cycle was 00Z through hour 360. Every available run covers the portion of the forecast for which it is used.

College of DuPage NEXLAB panels were inspected directly. Early-morning infrared imagery showed the frontal cloud shield across the northern part of the Southeast while the Upstate remained farther ahead of it. The radar mosaic showed no organized echoes over either forecast point at the check, consistent with rain arriving later rather than already occurring at issuance.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

Verification feedback through 2026-09-29 was consulted. Central Kentucky nighttime ranges were shifted modestly lower where the KDVK bias applies; Upstate highs were tempered and overnight ranges widened downward for KLQK. Day-three ranges were kept wider because historical 72-hour coverage is weakest, and residual low precipitation chances were not rounded down to near zero because the 0–20% reliability bin has verified wetter than forecast.
Radar and satellite links remain external and live; the existing Google Sites radar section is not modified by this candidate.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted overnight ranges about 1–2°F lower where the KDVK low-temperature signal applies and widened the Sunday-night range because historical 72-hour coverage is weakest. Daytime highs remain centered on current guidance because KLEX does not share the smaller KDVK daytime bias.

Tempered daytime ceilings and widened nighttime ranges downward to represent KLQK's recurring cold-pocket behavior. The full station-specific KLQK correction was not imposed across the entire Clemson region.
Retained nonzero residual precipitation probabilities where uncertainty exists because the verified 0–20% bin has observed precipitation more often than forecast.
